synopsis: A program starting in October 2026 can realistically have a parameterized machine-and-brake model and executable SIL regression framework by mid-2027, provided software interfaces can be defined; the under-four-month product-validation window is distinct from brake-model validation [f67, f840, f12208]. Off-road braking follows the same underlying physics as road braking but differs in magnitude and dominant influences, including payload, grades, deformable ground, thermal limits and drivetrain braking; published brake-response latencies span 0.3–2.5 seconds [f5886, f5888, f239]. Machine types and brake systems remain unconfirmed, and models do not transfer automatically across machine families; articulated steering, moving payloads and deformable surfaces require more than a simple braking model [f5863, f10430, f5885]. SIL and data-injection HIL cannot establish actual brake-chain behavior when that chain is modeled, so safety evidence requires real-machine anchoring, with VIL or proving-ground stops for each machine braking class and measurement of both brake requests and physical responses [f531, f5287, f770, f5558, f5640]. Brake-plant capability remains subject to ISO 3450 where applicable, but no published off-road automatic-braking stopping-distance model tolerance was found; small simulated clearance margins are not robust when comparable to geometry, friction, timing and brake-model uncertainties [f2340, f7808, f4343].

relations.note: Both state that machine dynamics, brakes and sensing do not transfer across machine families.
Both distinguish off-road braking magnitude and dominant influences from road braking.
Both report absent qualification of generative world models for soil and braking physics.
Both retain ISO 3450 obligations for the brake plant.
Adds executable regression, fault injection and software-interface conditions to the mid-2027 model milestone.
Extends SIL's physical-brake limitation to data-injection HIL with modeled machinery.
Specifies VIL or proving-ground stops per braking class as real-machine anchors.
Closed-loop SIL and HIL require brake-model validation through physical machine stops.
Recording commands and measured brake response supplies evidence for real-machine anchoring.
Physical stopping influences justify machine-specific model content, including soil, payload and brake delays.
The glossary identifies an articulated hauler's hinge as a specific simple-model limitation.
Configuration-dependent braking outcomes justify treating each brake and control integration separately.
Correlation invalidation after configuration changes reinforces the need to demonstrate family-extreme bounding.
Uncertain near-clearance stops justify explicit machine-specific brake and calibration uncertainty margins.
Barrick's stopping-zone factors corroborate speed, reaction, braking and machine-envelope components.
Deformable-surface limitations justify high-fidelity soil modeling for braking-sensitive cases.
Research linking degraded brakes to runaway risk supports degraded-braking safety-case coverage.
Perfect sensing cannot compensate for incorrect dynamics, supporting separate brake-model qualification.
